explanation: When the ground shook, a ball dropped from one of eight dragons' mouths into a bronze toad below, said to point towards the quake.

claims.text: In AD 132 Zhang Heng built a seismoscope, an instrument to detect distant earthquakes.
Zhang Heng's instrument of AD 132 was not built to detect eclipses, storms or underground water.
The instrument had eight dragons, each holding a ball that could drop into the mouth of a bronze toad below.
The dropped ball was said to show the direction of the earthquake.
